releaseNotes: v1.9.7: Proxy-pool egress is now enforced for every proxy type — a pool that is assigned but dead, disabled or unparsable fails before the first byte is sent instead of quietly answering from the host IP, Test Connection for edge pools runs through the relay with the same headers as chat traffic, and the relay types are defined in exactly one place. Transient 502/503/504 are now retried with upstream's own policy (3 attempts, 2s apart, no 429 retry), so an opencode-zen turn no longer dies on the first service_overloaded while the next attempt would have been served. opencode-zen (ocz) is a real executor with per-model format routing across /chat/completions, /messages and /responses, relay headers intact, and a quota tracker — previously it fell through to a generic forward and its accounts never showed in the dashboard. Usage and fallback log lines now name the account and print egress= as the pool name, not a UUID. Quota refresh makes one attempt per request, skips providers with no refresher, rotates Kiro credentials into apiKey, and parks accounts whose refresh token was revoked instead of warning on every panel open; the tracker fetches all accounts per pass with a cancellable bounded fan-out. Security: the x-9r-password header is honoured only on the one path whose handler verifies it, closing unauthenticated shutdown, self-update and OAuth auto-import. The updater falls through to the release's SHA256SUMS.txt when the manifest carries no digest, so '9router-go update' installs again. Known limits: Vercel edge relays still 504 on turns whose first token arrives after ~25s, and a genuinely saturated upstream still returns 503 after the retries.
